articles.title: Chalked Paint
articles.summary: Powdery chalky colour, blotchy oxidised patches and pinholes, dead matte with faint dusty sparkle. Reads as a faded, dusty, blotchy version of whatever colour you give it, like old barn paint gone chalky; matte with no shine.
articles.what: Oxidised paint gone to chalk — powdery blotches fading your colour, pinholed all over. Up close: Chalky pale ground with branching, squiggly darker patches 20-70 px wide, like peeled or faded oxidised paint, dotted with tiny pinholes. Shown on a neutral grey input, so the pale-and-dark grey here is not its colour: it takes your colour and fades it to a powdery tint, with the blotches darker. From a distance: Reads as a faded, dusty, blotchy version of whatever colour you give it, like old barn paint gone chalky; matte with no shine. Measured spec (average): metal 1, roughness 141, coat 119. Shine: semi-matte. Metal: none. It takes the colour you give the zone.
when: Fits: dirt late model, truck / off-road, stock car.
how: Click the zone you want to change.
Click the BASE MATERIAL box (it says "Click to choose a base") and type "Chalked Paint" in the SEARCH FINISHES box.
Click it to open the big preview, then click Apply.
Pick your colour with BASE COLOR.
Render and judge it on the car, not on the swatch.
tips: Hood, roof and tops: oxidation shows where the sun hits
Body sides for a full barn-find look
Dark numbers read well on the pale faded surface; pale numbers fade out.
Rust or patina streaks: fit the oxidised story
Pairs well with: rust, cast iron, cream, brown.
pitfalls: Not a clean flat matte: it has visible blotches and pinholes
Not rust: it fades the colour, no orange tones
Avoid: dirt and dust in the sim hide the blotches; weak under bright light.
articles.spec_character: Average spec: metal 1 (non-metal paint), roughness 141 (semi-matte), clearcoat 119 (satin or weak clearcoat). The spec is textured, not flat: roughness and clearcoat vary by 20 or more across the surface.
articles.intent_note: Full-finish shelf: the finish carries both its own paint look and its own shine.
articles.paint_advice: Gloss shows the paint colour as it is, so any colour works; pick the colour for contrast with the neighbouring zones, not for the finish. Avoid: dirt and dust in the sim hide the blotches; weak under bright light.

combos.why: Patterns that suit it: rust or patina streaks: fit the oxidised story; faded stripes and stencil lettering: look like old sign paint
Patterns to avoid: clean glossy graphics: contradict the dead matte; fine glitter patterns: out of character
Spec overlays that work: rough matte spec patches: reinforce chalky dryness; small gloss scuffs: look like rubbed-through chalk
Judge the paint and the shine together: the same spec looks different under different colours.

Shown in grey because it takes your colour; the crystals will be lighter and darker versions of whatever colour you. From a distance: Reads as your colour broken into a shattered mosaic of light and dark facets with a metallic glitter; like hot-dip zinc but tinted. Measured spec (average): metal 212, roughness 70, coat 93. Shine: satin. Metal: high. It takes the colour you give the zone.
when: Fits: truck / off-road, dirt late model, stock car.
how: Click the zone you want to change.
Click the BASE MATERIAL box (it says "Click to choose a base") and type "Galvanized Spangle" in the SEARCH FINISHES box.
Click it to open the big preview, then click Apply.
Pick your colour with BASE COLOR.
Render and judge it on the car, not on the swatch.
tips: Hood, sides and bumpers: big crystals need broad panels
Use a solid roof or lower band to calm it
Busy; use bold black or white numbers with an outline on a solid plate; thin numbers vanish into the facets.
Wide solid stripes: calms the facets and gives number room
Pairs well with: black, gunmetal, orange, rust.
pitfalls: Not plain galvanized: this one takes your colour and has stronger brightness jumps between crystals
Not camo: facets are the same hue, only the brightness changes
Avoid: delicate pinstripes get lost, next to other busy patterns.
articles.spec_character: Average spec: metal 212 (true metallic), roughness 70 (satin gloss), clearcoat 93 (satin or weak clearcoat). The spec is textured, not flat: metal and roughness and clearcoat vary by 20 or more across the surface.
articles.intent_note: Full-finish shelf: the finish carries both its own paint look and its own shine.
articles.paint_advice: Metal takes on the paint colour: light and mid colours keep the sparkle, very dark colours swallow it. Avoid: delicate pinstripes get lost, next to other busy patterns.

combos.why: Patterns that suit it: wide solid stripes: calms the facets and gives number room; thin pinlines in black or white: tidy trim
Patterns to avoid: other crystal, camo or flake patterns: facet on facet; fine mesh: moire with the hairlines
Spec overlays that work: brushed spec: adds sheet-steel direction; gloss clearcoat sheet: sharper crystal edges
Judge the paint and the shine together: the same spec looks different under different colours.

articles.title: Glass Flake
articles.summary: Dense fine glass-flake surface, even glittery sheen in whatever colour you give it, faceted shards catching white light. Your colour with a dense, even glitter haze under a deep glossy clear, like show-car micro flake; from a distance it is a sparkly smooth colour with no pattern.
articles.what: Translucent glass shards suspended in clear — faceted, crazed, catching white light. Up close: Shown in grey because it takes your colour: a very fine static of 1-2 px light and dark specks over a mid tone, with a few brighter clumps; no shapes you can pick out at this size. The metal swings widely (std 96), so the bright specks are individual flakes that catch light. From a distance: Your colour with a dense, even glitter haze under a deep glossy clear, like show-car micro flake; from a distance it is a sparkly smooth colour with no pattern. Measured spec (average): metal 65, roughness 35, coat 41. Shine: high gloss. Metal: low. It takes the colour you give the zone.

Render and judge it on the car, not on the swatch.
tips: Hood, roof and doors: the sparkle needs open panels in sun
Works well on rounded fenders where flakes catch changing light
Fine grain hardly hurts numbers; bold numbers in any contrasting colour read, white numbers can sparkle out a little.
Wide stripes and graphics: stay crisp over such a fine grain
Pairs well with: deep black, candy red, chrome trim, white pearl.

articles.title: Gold Leaf
articles.summary: Crinkled gold leaf sheets laid over your colour, patchy metallic foil with lifted edges and dark seams. Reads as a gilded car with your colour glinting between the foil patches; at distance the patches form a busy gold-and-base-colour mix, mostly gold.
articles.what: Gold leaf laid in sheets over your colour, crinkled and lifting at the corners. Up close: Shown over a grey input, so the grey is your colour: irregular angular gold patches, 8-25px, sharp-cornered like torn foil, covering about 60 percent, with your colour showing through the gaps between them. Gold is a flat bright yellow-gold with a slight crinkle. From a distance: Reads as a gilded car with your colour glinting between the foil patches; at distance the patches form a busy gold-and-base-colour mix, mostly gold. Measured spec (average): metal 158, roughness 43, coat 44. Shine: high gloss. Metal: medium. It takes the colour you give the zone.
when: Best on: hero panel, hood, roof.
Fits: show car, gt / sports car.
how: Click the zone you want to change.
Click the BASE MATERIAL box (it says "Click to choose a base") and type "Gold Leaf" in the SEARCH FINISHES box.

Render and judge it on the car, not on the swatch.
tips: Hood, roof and doors: large panels show the patch shapes
Pair with a dark base for the most contrast
Large black or deep-colour numbers with a thick outline read; gold, yellow and cream numbers vanish.
Black or deep burgundy base colours: classic luxury gilding on dark
Pairs well with: deep burgundy, black, cream, emerald green.
pitfalls: Not smooth gold chrome: it is broken patches over a visible base colour
Not metalflake: patches are big torn foil pieces, not tiny chips
Avoid: small numbers get lost in the crinkle, don't cover whole car or it reads noisy.

Patterns to avoid: camo: clutter; other glitter or foil patterns: duplicate

articles.title: Hammered
articles.summary: Ball-peen hammered metal, a lattice of round dents each catching its own highlight, in whatever colour you give it. Reads as a fine dimpled, beaten-metal surface with a busy sparkly shimmer; the individual dents blur into a glittery orange-peel-on-metal texture, and the cloudy patches give a slightly uneven polish.
articles.what: Ball-peen hammered metal — a lattice of dents, every facet catching its own light. Up close: A tight, very regular honeycomb lattice of small round bright dimples, each with a soft dark halo, packed edge to edge. Big soft light and dark clouds drift under the lattice, so some zones glow and others dim. Dimples are evenly sized, not random like real hammer marks. From a distance: Reads as a fine dimpled, beaten-metal surface with a busy sparkly shimmer; the individual dents blur into a glittery orange-peel-on-metal texture, and the cloudy patches give a slightly uneven polish. Measured spec (average): metal 224, roughness 39, coat 60. Shine: high gloss. Metal: full. It takes the colour you give the zone.
when: Fits: truck / off-road, dirt late model, show car.
how: Click the zone you want to change.
Click the BASE MATERIAL box (it says "Click to choose a base") and type "Hammered" in the SEARCH FINISHES box.
Click it to open the big preview, then click Apply.
Pick your colour with BASE COLOR.
Render and judge it on the car, not on the swatch.
tips: Doors and quarter panels: big flat areas show the dimple pattern
Hood: sparkles under sun, strong visual impact
Busy texture can hide thin numbers; use bold, high contrast or outlined numbers.
Wide bold stripes or big shapes: dimples are small so large graphics read cleanly over them
Pairs well with: copper, gunmetal, rust brown, matte black.
pitfalls: Not metal flake: dimples are regular round dents with halos, not random sparkle dots
Not golf-ball texture: dents are much finer and tightly packed
Avoid: dents fight with sharp graphics, dark colours swallow the highlights.
articles.spec_character: Average spec: metal 224 (true metallic), roughness 39 (high gloss), clearcoat 60 (strong-to-medium clearcoat). The spec is textured, not flat: metal and roughness and clearcoat vary by 20 or more across the surface.
articles.intent_note: Full-finish shelf: the finish carries both its own paint look and its own shine.
articles.paint_advice: Metal takes on the paint colour: light and mid colours keep the sparkle, very dark colours swallow it. Avoid: dents fight with sharp graphics, dark colours swallow the highlights.

combos.why: Patterns that suit it: wide bold stripes or big shapes: dimples are small so large graphics read cleanly over them; outline logos and thick numbers backgrounds: the busy texture needs strong contrast to be read
Patterns to avoid: fine carbon, weave or glitter: stacks busy on busy and turns to mush; thin pinstripes: the dent lattice breaks up small details
Spec overlays that work: soft clearcoat haze: calms the sparkle into satin hammered metal; directional brushed streaks: adds an anisotropic glint across the dimples
Judge the paint and the shine together: the same spec looks different under different colours.

articles.title: Holo Flake
articles.summary: Pale cream-grey holographic flake, thousands of tiny flakes each flashing its own faint rainbow, bright and shimmering. A fine sparkling dust that tints the paint with pink-white twinkle; the muddy field underneath is just the render tint, the real colour is whatever you put under it.
articles.what: Holographic glitter vinyl — thousands of flakes, each one its own rainbow order. Up close: Dense micro glitter: thousands of single-pixel to 3 px flakes, most pink and white with a few dark pits, scattered at random over a flat muddy field. No cells, no direction, no big shapes; every flake is its own tiny bright dot. From a distance: A fine sparkling dust that tints the paint with pink-white twinkle; the muddy field underneath is just the render tint, the real colour is whatever you put under it. Measured spec (average): metal 204, roughness 12, coat 26. Shine: mirror. Metal: high. It brings its own colours.
when: Best on: body, roof, hero panel.
Fits: show car, gt / sports car, open wheel.
how: Click the zone you want to change.
Click the BASE MATERIAL box (it says "Click to choose a base") and type "Holo Flake" in the SEARCH FINISHES box.
Click it to open the big preview, then click Apply.
Leave BASE COLOR on Use finish's own color to keep its colours.
Render and judge it on the car, not on the swatch.
tips: Hood, roof, trunk: large areas where the glitter flashes
Side panels: gloss and flake show best on gentle curves
Solid dark or bold numbers stay readable; light numbers can be eaten by the sparkle.
Large bold stripes or blocks: flakes show through as texture in the shapes
Pairs well with: black, white, purple, chrome.
pitfalls: Not pearl: pearl shifts colour smoothly, this is separate hard-edged flakes
Not standard metallic flake: it is sparklier and many flakes read pink/white
Avoid: numbers, next to other loud finishes.
articles.spec_character: Average spec: metal 204 (true metallic), roughness 12 (razor or mirror smooth), clearcoat 26 (very strong clearcoat). The spec is textured, not flat: metal and clearcoat vary by 20 or more across the surface.
articles.intent_note: Full-finish shelf: the finish carries both its own paint look and its own shine.
articles.paint_advice: It brings its own colours, so leave BASE COLOR on the finish's own colour. Put it next to a plain zone of the opposite sheen (matte beside gloss, warm beside cool) so the colours have a calm neighbour. Avoid: numbers, next to other loud finishes.

combos.why: Patterns that suit it: large bold stripes or blocks: flakes show through as texture in the shapes; big soft gradients or fades: the glitter rides cleanly across the colour change
Patterns to avoid: fine metallic, hex or sparkle patterns: compete with the flake and read as noise; dense camo: loses both
Spec overlays that work: broad gloss clearcoat: deepens the glitter like vinyl under a lacquer; coarse metallic ripple: adds big shimmer under the flake
Judge the paint and the shine together: the same spec looks different under different colours.
